subject.title: Subagent sessions persist after completion, main session becomes unresponsive

question: What should OpenClaw’s default terminal one-shot subagent retention and visibility contract be?
rationale: The code has several plausible repair paths, but changing default cleanup or hiding retained child sessions changes user-visible history, attachment retention, task status, and operator recovery semantics.

options.title: Archive/hide terminal one-shot subagents by default
options.body: Keep enough recent history for debugging but stop completed one-shot children from appearing active or blocking parent/session status surfaces after a defined retention window.

options.title: Delete terminal one-shot subagents by default
options.body: Remove run-mode child session rows and attachments after successful delivery unless callers explicitly request `cleanup=keep`, at the cost of less default history.

options.title: Preserve current retention and improve diagnostics only
options.body: Leave child rows visible by default and focus on making UI, status, and task surfaces distinguish retained history from active work.

recommendation.title: Archive/hide terminal one-shot subagents by default
recommendation.body: Keep enough recent history for debugging but stop completed one-shot children from appearing active or blocking parent/session status surfaces after a defined retention window.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses subagent registry, gateway session listing, task maintenance, and product retention semantics, and this person has recent broad history across those paths.
